"You are an experienced game developer and game designer. I'm building a Durango-style dinosaur survival game. Design the project and write the code for [Engine: Unity C# / Unreal / Godot / Web (JS) — pick one] based on the spec below.

■ CORE SYSTEMS
1. Survival Stats
- Health, hunger (satiety), and thirst decrease over time
- Restore via water (rivers/lakes/purified) and food (berries, meat, cooked meals)
- At 0, health drains continuously; low values reduce movement speed and attack power
- Raw food restores little; cooking increases efficiency

2. Dinosaur Taming
- Per-species temperament (herbivore/carnivore/neutral); stages: Wild → Wary → Curious → Tamed
- Fill an affinity gauge by feeding preferred food or weakening the creature
- Tamed dinosaurs: rideable, carry loads, assist in combat, assist in gathering
- Each dinosaur has its own hunger, loyalty, and level
- At least 5 species (e.g., Triceratops, Raptor, Brachiosaurus, Pteranodon, Tyrannosaurus)

3. Leveling / Progression
- XP from hunting, gathering, crafting, building → level up → skill points
- Skill trees: Gathering, Combat, Crafting, Taming, Survival
- Recipes and buildings unlock by level

4. Building
- Grid-based placement: floor, wall, door, roof, workbench, furnace, storage chest, bed
- Material tiers: leaves/wood → stone → iron
- Demolition, repair, durability; dinosaur pens (fences)

5. Crafting
- Tools/weapons: stone axe, spear, bow, crossbow, iron sword, etc.
- Craftable lists per workbench type, material consumption, durability
- Resources: wood, stone, fiber, ore, leather, bone

6. World
- Procedurally generated map (forest, plains, desert, lake)
- Day/night cycle, weather, biome-specific dinosaur and resource distribution
- Respawn system

■ REQUIREMENTS
1. First present the overall architecture (folder/class design, data table structure)
2. Then implement one system at a time (Survival Stats → Inventory/Crafting → Building → Dinosaur AI/Taming → Level/Skills)
3. Separate all balance values into external data (ScriptableObject/JSON, etc.) for easy tuning
4. Include comments and testing instructions with every piece of code
5. One system per response; continue when I say \"next\"

Start with step 1: the architecture design.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.
"
